newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's government tumbles in popularity poll.
newsitem.headline: Spain's government tumbles in popularity poll.

text.p: Spain's opposition Socialist Workers Party has dislodged the five-month-old conservative government from the top of a key popularity poll for the first time since the new government was elected.

The quarterly survey published by the daily El Pais on Monday, showed the Socialists (PSOE) now lead the ruling Partido Popular (PP) by 4.6 points, with 27.8 percent saying they would vote for the PSOE in the next election.
In the previous poll conducted in July, the government led the PSOE by 5.9 points, with 30.5 percent saying they would vote for the PP in the next election.

The autumn survey revealed that 59 percent of those polled thought the government had not fulfilled its election promises and 63 percent said they believed Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar was impulsive in making policy.
The survey of 1,200 adults conducted between October 7 and 9, also found that 40 percent disapproved of the performance of the government so far, compared with 31 percent who approved.
The results come as a great contrast to July's poll when Aznar topped the survey for the first time, beating the perennial favourite Socialist leader Felipe Gonzalez.
But in October's poll, Gonzalez was back in poll position, scoring 5.1 out of 10 compared with 4.7 out of 10 for Aznar.
The survey by polling agency Demoscopia has a margin error of 2.9 percent.
